chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali or someone else, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

A boy who had not yet reached puberty sneezed in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he said, 'The Praise is for Allah.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'May Allah place blessings in you.'

key_terms.بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكَ: May Allah place blessings in you

ai.seo_question: What is the proper response when someone sneezes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practice of responding to a young boy’s sneeze with 'Baraka Allahu fik' (May Allah bless you), demonstrating that the etiquette of sneezing applies across age groups. Shia scholars emphasize this as a confirmation of the Sunnah’s universality, showing that even pre-pubescent children are included in the communal rituals of praise and blessing. The incident underscores the gentle and inclusive nature of the Prophet’s teachings, where spiritual etiquette is instilled from early childhood.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, or someone else, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘A boy who had yet to reach puberty, sneezed in the presence of the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, and he said, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’. So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said to him: ‘May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Place Blessings in you’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from al- Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
A young boy who had not yet reached puberty once sneezed in the presence of the Holy Prophet and said, ‘All praise belongs to Allah.’ The Holy Prophet said, ‘May Allah place blessings in you.’”
